mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 8% signals a deepening recession, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals labor market strength that boosts corporate earnings expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 200,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and real personal savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during co-activation of HOUST and RSAFS above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 3% while the federal funds rate remains below 1% for three consecutive months, it signals insufficient monetary tightening relative to inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS < 1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) to below 5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth accelerates above 3% per month for two months signals a tight labor market that raises wage inflation and cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% AND PAYEMS growth > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such tight labor market signals.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a macroeconomic recession, which causes a sustained reduction in corporate earnings and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive quarterly GDP declines.
